items.behavior: Reachy reacts with an appropriate emotion move during conversation while continuing to track the speaker
items.verification: Live run: 'I got the job!' triggers excited-class move layered on tracking anchor
items.evidence: automated pass 2026-08-17 on mockup-sim (task-91011 logs: task-91011-app.err.log, task-91011-rpc.jsonl): injected '我升职了！恭喜我吧！' via conversation.say -> play_emotion tool call at +618 ms with celebratory intent args={"emotion":"excited"} -> resolve_emotion_name mapped it to recorded move 'dance3' (model-visible result {'status': 'queued', 'emotion': 'dance3'}) -> MovementManager accepted it ('Queued move with duration 18.36s, queue size: 1' + 'Stopping breathing due to new move activity') -> idle breathing resumed automatically ('Started breathing after 18.4s of inactivity'), i.e. the move ran to completion and idle behaviour came back. scripts/preload_assets.py ran clean beforehand (exit 0, 6 'cached:' lines + 'done', 2.6 s on a warm HF cache). NOTE: the model answered with the emotion ONLY and spoke no words for this turn (play_emotion has needs_response=False), and dance3 is an 18.4 s move. OPERATOR PASS PENDING: that the move reads as celebratory on the real robot, that 18.4 s is acceptable demo pacing (or a shorter intent is preferred), whether a silent celebration is the wanted behaviour, and that the emotion visibly layers over live face tracking (untestable on mockup-sim, see US-02).
items.next: Task 15 operator run: judge move suitability/duration and the silent-celebration behaviour

items.behavior: User shows an object; Reachy captures a frame and describes it correctly
items.verification: Live run: 'What am I holding?' with 3 different objects, 3/3 correct
items.evidence: automated pass 2026-08-17 on mockup-sim (task-91011 logs): injected '你现在看到了什么？请先用相机看一下再回答。' -> full image chain verified end to end: camera tool call at +1745 ms (args question='你现在看到了什么？请描述眼前的场景和明显物体。') -> frame grabbed in 28 ms -> sanitized model-visible result {'image_attached': True} -> separate input_image conversation item created and ACCEPTED by gpt-realtime-2.1 ('Added camera image to conversation jpeg_bytes=32745', response.created 250 ms later) -> spoken description at +5334 ms. NO API error of any kind: the Task 10 Step 2 contingency (model rejecting the image item) did NOT trigger, so openai_realtime.py needs no image-shape fix. Spoken transcript: '我这边看到的是一片黑，像是镜头前很暗，或者被挡住了。看不清具体物体或场景。你要不要稍微挪一下相机，或者打开灯？' — an accurate reading of the frame it was given, but the frame carried no usable scene: mockup-sim builds its camera with autovideosrc (media_server.py:883 _build_autovideo_source, 'MOCKUP uses autovideosrc') with no device selection, which resolved to ksvideosrc -> first enumerated camera, and this host enumerates 'IR Camera' ahead of 'FHD Webcam' — a dark, noisy IR frame (32.7 KB JPEG = noise, not a flat black image). Dev-box/mockup-sim artifact only: the real robot selects its camera by name (media_server.py _build_windows_source/_build_linux_source via find_video_device). OPERATOR PASS PENDING: the actual 3-objects-3/3-correct check, which needs a human holding objects to a camera that sees a lit RGB scene.
items.next: Task 15 operator run: 3 objects on the robot camera; image plumbing already proven

items.behavior: Question about today's news triggers automatic web search without being asked to search
items.verification: Live run: 'What happened with NVIDIA today?' → search tool call visible in logs → current answer
items.evidence: automated pass 2026-08-17 on mockup-sim (task-91011 logs): injected '今天英伟达有什么新闻？' with NO mention of searching -> the model chose the search tool unprompted at +1895 ms, tool_name='pollen_robotics_reachy_mini_search_tool__search_web' args={"query":"今天 英伟达 新闻","max_results":5}. HF Space route SUCCEEDED (no auth failure, no error): MCP streamable-http to https://pollen-robotics-reachy-mini-search-tool.hf.space/gradio_api/mcp/ returned a result envelope {'status': 'ok', 'server_alias': 'pollen_robotics_reachy_mini_search_tool', 'remote_tool_name': 'reachy_mini_search_tool_search_web', 'content_blocks': [...]} carrying real dated Chinese results (e.g. '英伟达押注文远知行，广州AI...' on the Robotaxi/Orin investment). Spoken answer reflected that current info (自动驾驶/Robotaxi 投资合作、新模型或芯片能力、估值走势) with an honest caveat about source freshness. LATENCY (the Step 2 trigger is 'fails OR too slow' — it did not fail): say -> final spoken answer 16.8 s, of which the tool occupied 6.9 s, and only 2.4 s of that was the actual tools/call search; the other 4.5 s is per-call MCP session overhead — initialize 1.63 s + notifications/initialized 1.04 s + a trailing, post-result tools/list 1.07 s + 0.51 s connect. The session is torn down and rebuilt for every invocation. Fallback NOT implemented in this run (out of scope, reported for the controller's decision); note that session reuse would cut ~4.5 s without changing the route. OPERATOR PASS PENDING: same turn spoken to a live mic on the robot, and a judgement on whether 16.8 s to a spoken answer is acceptable demo pacing.
items.next: controller decision on Task 11 Step 2: route works, so the only open question is latency — prefer MCP session reuse over the Tavily fallback

items.behavior: Face tracking is active continuously from app startup, with no model tool call required
items.verification: Dev + robot run: tracking active immediately after launch; log shows no head_tracking tool call
items.evidence: automated pass 2026-08-17 on mockup-sim (task-91011 logs): NO head_tracking tool call anywhere in a 6-minute DEBUG-level run — the only occurrences of the name are tool registration ('Found 12 tools to load', 'Loaded core tool: head_tracking', 'tool registered'), never 'Tool call received — tool_name=head_tracking'. Daemon-side tracking was nevertheless already RUNNING before anything was asked of it, proven by a CPU A/B on the daemon worker process (pid 4480) after the three evidence turns: as-left-by-the-app 10.4% of a core -> POST /api/media/tracking/disable -> 6.1% -> POST /api/media/tracking/enable -> 8.2%. The as-left state matches the explicitly-enabled state and is ~40% above the disabled state, so the YuNet FaceTracker thread the app started at boot (main.py:374 movement_manager.set_head_tracking(True) -> moves.py:380 start_head_tracking(weight=1.0)) was genuinely active; no 'Head-tracking toggle failed' warning app-side and no 'Cannot enable head tracking: no camera available' warning daemon-side. GET /api/media/tracking/face answered 200 on all 7 polls but always with face_target {detected:false,x:null,y:null,roll:null,ts:null} — and that endpoint is STRUCTURALLY DEAD on mockup-sim: _face_target is only ever written by step_head_tracking(), which is called solely from daemon/backend/robot/backend.py:249; the mockup_sim run loop (mockup_sim/backend.py:73) never calls it, so no face can ever be reported and the head never actually aims on the dev box. What the webcam saw is moot for the same reason, and was in any case the host's IR camera (see DEMO-3). OPERATOR PASS PENDING: the live-face half — that the head visibly follows a real face from startup on the real robot, where step_head_tracking() does run.
items.next: Task 15 operator run: confirm the head visibly follows a live face from startup (mockup-sim cannot show this)
